title: OpenAI Seals New Pacts to Deploy AI Across UAE Energy and Investment Sectors
summary:
OpenAI has expanded its partnership with Abu Dhabi through new agreements to integrate generative AI into the operations of the emirate's state-owned companies and public services. The pacts include a deal to make ADNOC the first energy company to use OpenAI's Frontier technology for oil production and trading decisions, as well as a collaboration with investment firm Mubadala to apply AI to risk assessment and opportunity analysis. Other arrangements include a five year partnership with Inception42 and a project to convert government regulations into machine-readable formats to automate compliance checks.

The expansion occurs as CEO Sam Altman visits the UAE and OpenAI pursues billions of dollars in investment from state-backed funders. In addition to the software deployments, the AI firm is involved in the development of a 5 GW AI data center in the region, further strengthening ties with the government's goal of creating a fully AI-native administration.

selectedTweets.text:
OpenAI has signed 4 new agreements in Abu Dhabi as CEO Sam Altman visits the UAE, expanding its presence across energy, government and investment.

The agreements include:

1) ADNOC + G42: ADNOC becomes the first energy company to deploy OpenAI's Frontier technology, using AI to improve decisions across oil production, refining and trading.

2) Abu Dhabi Government: OpenAI will help convert government regulations into machine-readable formats, allowing AI to assist with permits and compliance checks. The first pilot is already live.

3) Mubadala + Inception42: Deploying AI for investment analysis, identifying opportunities and assessing risks.

4) Inception42: A five-year partnership to expand OpenAI's technology across government agencies, businesses and education in the UAE.

The deals deepen OpenAI's ties with the UAE, where it is also involved in a planned 5 GW AI data center project.
